<thought>The mass spectrum shows a Br isotopic pattern (M and M+2 of similar intensity) with a molecular ion around 199 Da, indicating a single bromine atom. The ¹H NMR displays two equivalent aromatic double‑double‑doublets (2 H each) typical of a para‑disubstituted benzene, and two aliphatic triplets (2 H each, J ≈ 7 Hz) consistent with a –CH₂‑CH₂‑ fragment attached to the ring. The simplest structure matching a para‑disubstituted bromobenzene with an ethyl substituent is 4‑bromo‑ethylbenzene. Its SMILES representation is:

`CCc1ccc(Br)cc1`

This SMILES yields the correct formula (C₈H₉Br) and reproduces the observed NMR pattern and bromine isotopic signature.</thought>
<final_answer>CCc1ccc(Br)cc1</final_answer>
